about: When inputs were made (sample/InputTimeProbe.tsx; input.h; docs/react-native-android-adaptation.mdx): React Native's touches and W3C pointer events carry the time the device reported each input, which the compositor sends with it (the protocol's time_us: libinput's event time, the development compositor's director giving its own), as Android's carry MotionEvent.getEventTime(), not the time they reached JavaScript. A double press made as a person makes one (the second press 150 ms after the first, oxyos-offscreen's DOUBLE_PRESS_MS) reaches the host at once, and its first press-in keeps JavaScript busy for 400 ms, a slow frame: the pad still tells a double press (within Android's 300 ms double-tap timeout) by the presses' timeStamp, 150 ms apart, the pointer downs' too, on performance.now()'s clock. On a 1600x1000 output at 1.25.

steps.name: one press: its touches and pointer events carry its time, on performance.now()'s clock
a double press behind a slow frame is still a double press: its presses were made 150 ms apart
